term: AI: When a Robot Writes a Play
definition: AI: When a Robot Writes a Play (in Czech: AI: Když robot píše hru) is a 2021 experimental theatre play, where 90% of its script was automatically generated by artificial intelligence (the GPT-2 language model).
details: The play is in Czech language, but an English version of the script also exists.

explainer.lead: AI: When a Robot Writes a Play is an experimental Czech theatre production whose script was written mainly by GPT-2, with a dramaturge guiding and editing the output. It offers a concrete demonstration of both what generative AI can contribute to creative writing and how much human work is still needed to turn its output into a performance.

tiers.eli5: Imagine making up a story with a robot that keeps suggesting what could happen next. A human writer gives it the start of each scene and chooses, rejects, or changes its suggestions, rather than letting it write completely alone. The finished play follows a robot through eight scenes about things such as death, fear, work, and love.
tiers.practitioner: The workflow used scene descriptions and opening character lines as prompts for THEaiTRobot, a GPT-2-based writing tool, with the dramaturge accepting, rejecting, partially using, or manually extending generations. The English script was translated into Czech with CUBBITT and then post-edited. Practical difficulties included inconsistent or nonsensical passages, substantial interpretive work by the theatre company, and generated sex, violence, strong language, and stereotyped characters.
tiers.paperLevel: The play was the first result of the THEaiTRE project, which investigated AI-generated theatre scripts for the centenary of Karel Čapek's R.U.R. For the English script, composition = 90% automatically generated text + 10% manually written or manually post-edited text; the Czech version received further corrections, principally for automated translation and style. Its limits include loose links between scenes, inconsistencies and nonsensical turns, and a heavy reliance on human editing, direction, and acting to produce a coherent interpretation.

explainer.example: In the second scene, the Robot meets an angry Boy and repeatedly refuses his requests for a joke before finally producing one: "When you are dead. When your children are dead. When your grandchildren are dead, I will be still alive." The moment shows how generated dialogue could become darkly comic while still depending on the surrounding human-written setup and the production's interpretation.

usedIn.name: THEaiTRE research project
usedIn.detail: The play was the project's first experiment in using artificial intelligence to create theatre scripts.

usedIn.name: Švanda Theatre
usedIn.detail: The Prague theatre participated in creating the script and premiered the play, directed by Daniel Hrbek.

usedIn.name: Non-commercial script use
usedIn.detail: The English and Czech scripts were made freely available for non-commercial use, with manual insertions and edits marked.

explainer.intuition: The process treats a language model as a prolific but unreliable co-writer: a human supplies dramatic structure and opening lines, and the model proposes continuations. Human selection, editing, translation correction, and stage interpretation turn those proposals into a performable play.
howItWorks: Dramaturge David Košťák described each scene's initial setting and wrote the first line for each character.
THEaiTRobot, based on GPT-2, suggested continuations of the script.
Košťák could accept, reject, partly reuse, or replace a suggestion and add lines or scenic remarks himself.
CUBBITT automatically translated the generated English script into Czech.
The dramaturge post-edited the result, and Švanda Theatre developed its stage interpretation.
explainer.whyItMatters: The production made human–AI collaboration in scriptwriting publicly visible and measurable, including how much of the English text was generated. Its awkward passages and dependence on directors and actors also illustrate why fluent text generation is not the same as producing a coherent, meaningful play.
misconceptions: The AI did not create the entire play independently; people supplied setups and opening lines, selected and edited text, and shaped the performance.
GPT-2 generated the script in English, not directly in Czech; CUBBITT translated it before further human editing.
Ninety percent generation does not imply a polished script: reviewers noted inconsistencies, nonsensical sections, and the need for extensive stage interpretation.
